properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: jsonwebtoken@9.0.2 pinned in samples-classic/javascript/quickstart package-lock.json and PyJWT in two requirements.txt files — the JWT signing stacks the samples ship. jsonwebtoken/PyJWT default to HS256 (HMAC-SHA256) signing, a symmetric MAC — quantum-safe-ish against Shor but Grover-affected; the libraries can also emit RS256/ES256 (Shor-vulnerable) when the caller picks an asymmetric alg. The default-credential samples here use these libraries to mint bearer tokens for A

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X.509 certificate handling in the C# egress-control sample: builds an X509Certificate2Collection of trusted roots and validates the server certificate presented during egress against them — a custom chain-validation gate for outbound traffic. The underlying signature algorithms (RSA/ECDSA, typically Shor-vulnerable) are whatever the presented chain carries; this code is the verification point, changeable here in the sense that ML-DSA chain validation would need a runtime that supports it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: jsonwebtoken pinned in the package-lock.json of the JS quickstart (samples-classic) and 10 other JS/TS sample lockfiles. This is the JWT sign/verify stack shipped by the samples; its default HS256 (HMAC-SHA256) is a MAC, and it can emit RS256/ES256 (Shor-vulnerable asymmetric) when configured. Changeable here at the dependency level.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: jws@3.2.2 pinned in samples-classic/javascript/quickstart — the JWS sign/verify layer under jsonwebtoken. Same logical dependency as the jws LIB object (two collector rules, one package); jws exposes HS*/RS*/ES* algs, the asymmetric ones Shor-vulnerable when selected.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: jwa@1.4.2 in samples-classic/javascript/quickstart — the JOSE algorithm registry (HMAC-SHA256/384, RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, ECDSA, PBES2 key management) under jws/jsonwebtoken. Same logical dependency as the jwa LIB object. The ES256/RS256 branches are Shor-vulnerable when the caller selects them.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: httpx@0.28.1 declared by the private-ca-recovery scripts — the HTTPS client carrying the agent export/restore traffic. Its TLS group/cipher policy comes from the ambient OpenSSL, unpinned in-tree, so key agreement is classical ECDHE unless the runtime is OpenSSL ≥3.5.
